co_interiors_wall_area.blurb: Interiors Wall is the busiest cliff in Escalante Canyon, a quiet crack-climbing canyon on sandstone roughly twenty miles south of Grand Junction. It sits on the right as you enter public land, a short walk up from the road. Nearly all of its 22 climbs are single-pitch trad cracks, with a lone boulder problem thrown in. Grades start around 5.6 and top out in the low 5.12s, but most lines fall between 5.8 and 5.11, so mid-grade crack climbers get the most out of it. A large cave holds several crack lines on its back wall. The sandstone weakens badly when damp, so give it a day or two to dry after rain, and bring a full rack.

co_main_canyon.blurb: Main Canyon is the principal climbing sector of Witches' Canyon, just southwest of Penitente Canyon in the San Luis Valley. Almost all of its 22 climbs are bolted sport lines on fine-grained volcanic tuff, 30 to 50 feet tall, with a pair of trad cracks and one boulder problem mixed in. Difficulty leans toward the 5.10s and 5.11s, backed by a solid group of 5.12s and a few 5.13 and 5.14 test pieces, so it suits strong climbers more than beginners. The canyon floor is well forested, which brings welcome shade on hot days. Climbing begins soon after you park, so walks are minimal.

co_east_buttress.blurb: East Buttress is the smaller cliff east of the main Ophir Wall, near Telluride at roughly 9,000 feet. It holds 22 routes in a fairly even trad and sport split. Grades run from 5.7 up into the low 5.13s; most lines are 5.8 to 5.11, while the harder sport routes gather on an upper tier known as the Jungle Gym, and a gully higher up mixes sport, trad and mixed lines. Ophir is known for solid grades, technical movement and the occasional runout, so expect old-school character rather than plush bolting. Reaching it means crossing the boulder fields below the main wall, about a quarter hour from the parking area.

co_swan_mountain_road.blurb: Swan Mountain Road is a modest bouldering spot in the Keystone area of Summit County, centred on a long traverse wall with a scattering of individual boulders nearby. Most of the 22 climbs are boulder problems, with a handful of short top-rope routes and a couple of trad lines. The difficulty is gentle: problems are mainly VB through V3, with one standout much harder, and the top-ropes are mostly low 5th class. It is a good place to build endurance on easy ground, and the wall stays shady and cool in summer. A trail leads in from the parking area and the traverse wall appears after roughly five to eight minutes.

co_mary_s_bust_main_buttress.blurb: The main buttress is the big, steep face of Mary's Bust, standing on the north side of US 34 in Big Thompson Canyon about eight miles east of Estes Park. The rock is granitic, with quartz intrusions and pockets of mica. Of its 22 routes, 20 are bolted sport lines and two are trad, ranging from short single pitches to long outings of up to six pitches. Grades cluster in the 5.10s and 5.11s, with a few 5.12s and only a couple of easier options, so it favours solid intermediates and up. Sun is often warm here, though some shade can be found. Approaches are brief, but the rock is still shedding, so wear a helmet.
